summary: Study constructive natural-deduction proofs, their substitution operations, and exactly how excluded middle restores classical reasoning.
abstract: A proof of an implication can temporarily assume its antecedent and then discharge that assumption. This familiar operation remains available even when we stop accepting arbitrary proof by contradiction. Intuitionistic natural deduction keeps the introduction and elimination rules for each connective, including reasoning from a contradiction, while leaving out the classical contradiction rule. We prove that its finite proof trees can be weakened, combined, and uniformly substituted, and that negation can be expanded as implication to falsum. Several useful negation laws still have proofs, including double-negated excluded middle. Adding either excluded middle or double-negation elimination recovers exactly the classical deductions already studied.
